successors.name: Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu)
successors.text: the southern part of the Department of Amazonas, 'the triangular region formed by the confluence of the Marañón River and the Utcubamba in Bagua Province', 'up to the basin of the Abiseo River where…

ledger.x: c. 800: the Chachapoya culture begins. 'Started around the year 800 and continued until the conquest by the Inca in about 1470'.

c. 1470: the Inca conquer the Chachapoya. The page's overview says about 1470, a later section 'around 1475', Garcilaso the second half of the 15th century under Tupac Inca Yupanqui; garrisons and forced resettlement (mitma) followed and smaller rebellions continued.

c. 1470: Chachapoya independence ends. 'Some elements of the Cachapoya continued until the Spanish conquest'; Huaman of Quchapampa pledged allegiance to Pizarro after Atahualpa's capture (undated); 'by 1547' a Spanish faction was in the city of Chachapoyas.

wars.name: Inca conquest of the Chachapoya
wars.outcome: The Inca under Tupac Inca Yupanqui conquer the Chachapoya (about 1470, 'around 1475'); garrisons and mitma resettlement.

wars.name: Chachapoya rebellion against Huayna Capac
wars.outcome: Governors and ministers were killed; Huayna Capac attacked and crossed the Marañón on rafts; women at Cajamarquilla asked for mercy and the Inca granted peace.

certainty.note: No limits on the page; the redrawn pieces stand for river basins (Utcubamba, Abiseo) and a southward extension that no page bounds.
